```{r loading data}

#| label: load-data
#| include: false
library("reshape2")
library("ggplot2")
library("ggrain")

raw <-read.csv("data/raw/data_doctored.csv")
data <- raw[ ,c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth", "Relationship_status", 
                "Country_raised", "Individualism_col_1", 
                "Individualism_col_2", "Individualism_col_4", 
                "Relationship_length", "Love_how_much_1")]


```

```{r cleaning data}

data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]
data[, 5:7] <- apply(data[ , 5:7], 2, function(x) {
  ifelse(x <1 | x > 7, NA, x)
})

#codebook: 0 = Male, 1 = Female, 2 = Intersex
table(data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")

#turn sex_birth into a factor with labels Male, Female, and Intersex
data$Sex_birth <- factor(data$Sex_birth,
                         levels = c(0,1,2),
                         labels = c("Male","Female","Intersex"))

table(data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")

```

## Hypothesis 1: Germany and USA participants differ in levels of individualism

### Variables:

**Country raised (Country_raised)**: a categorical variable defining where participants were raised, in this case only looking at participants who respond with "Germany" or "United States"

**Individualism**: a composite variable compiled of three separate individualist/collectivist-determining questions (Individualism_col_1, Individualism_col_2, Individualism_col_4) that were reverse-scored.

```{r individualism}

## checking if numeric
is.numeric(data[,5])
is.numeric(data[,6])
is.numeric(data[,7])

# making these columns numeric
data[,5:7] <- lapply(data[,5:7], as.numeric)

# creating a total account of individualist questions
data$individualistTotal <- rowSums(data[,5:7],na.rm=FALSE)

# create reversed mean of individualist to measure individualism
data$individualism <- 8 - (rowMeans(data[ , 5:7], na.rm = TRUE))
## NOW: higher === greater individualism; lower == greater collectivism

```

```{r}

#| label: h1-descriptives

summary (data[, c("individualism", "Country_raised")])

```

## H1 Graph

```{r H1 graphing}

# data set that just includes people raised in Germany or the USA
GermanyUSAData <- data[data$Country_raised %in% c("Germany", "USA"), ]


H1Rain <- ggplot(data = GermanyUSAData,
                 aes(x = Country_raised,
                     y = individualism,
                     fill = Country_raised)) +
  labs(x = "Raised in Germany versus USA",
       y = "Level of Individualism",
       fill = "Germany vs USA") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Gernany", "USA")) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("Germany", "USA")) +
  geom_rain(alpha=.5) 

H1Rain


```

## Hypothesis 2: Length of relationship influences present feelings of love

### Variables:

**Length of relationship (Relationship_length)**: length of current relationship for participants in committed relationships, measured in years.

**Feelings of love (Love_how_much_1)**: how much a participant loves their romantic partner, if they are in a committed relationship.

```{r}

#| label: h2-descriptives

summary (data[, c("Relationship_length", "Love_how_much_1")])

```

## H2 Graph

```{r}

H2Point <- ggplot(data = data,
                  aes(x = Relationship_length,
                      y = Love_how_much_1,
                      color = Relationship_length)) +
  labs(x = "Length of Romantic Relationship",
       y = "Length of Relationship (years)") +
  geom_jitter(width = .12, height = .04, alpha = .6, size = .6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  theme_gray(base_size = 8)

H2Point
```
